newsitem.title: USA: Dayton Target sales close to plan in May.
newsitem.headline: Dayton Target sales close to plan in May.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said sales at its Target discount store chain have met expectations or fallen slightly below plan so far in May.
"Target is on plan to very, very slightly below plan," said Dayton Hudson chief executive Bob Ulrich during a press conference after the company's annual meeting here.

Sales at Mervyn's, a mid-level department store chain, have been "slightly better than plan" in May, he said. The company's department store division, which includes Dayton's, Hudson's and Marshall Field's stores, has had sales that are "slightly below plan" in May.
Ulrich said cool spring weather could explain the slight weakness in Target's sales.
Linda Ahlers, president of the department store division, said sales of better womens' apparel has been strong, but moderately priced womens' apparel has been weaker.

Mervyn's, which posted flat same-store sales for the first quarter, has met the company's profit expectations, said Bart Butzer, president of Mervyn's. But the division will continue to work to post positive same-store sales this year.

One shareholder said he was disappointed with the new name that Dayton Hudson recently gave to its Mervyn's division, Mervyn's California. Ralph Cornelius, of St. Louis Park, Minn., said attaching "California" to Mervyn's name turns off people who don't live in that state.
"I think we're shooting ourselves in the foot in 49 states," Cornelius said.
Mervyn's has 276 stores in 15 Western and Midwestern states.
Dayton Hudson has conducted research that showed shoppers have a positive association with California, but the company is not wedded to the new name, Ulrich said.
"It's a legitimate point and it's something we'll keep looking at," he said.

Earlier this year, Mervyn's announced it would close or sell 10 stores and exit markets in Florida and Georgia. On Wednesday, Dayton Hudson said it does not expect to close more stores and has no plans to shed the division.
